newsitem.title: BELGIUM: No U.S. reply yet on EU's GATT rice offer.
newsitem.headline: No U.S. reply yet on EU's GATT rice offer.

text.p: The United States has not yet replied to new proposals from the European Commission on tendering arrangements for a controversial new GATT rice quota, a Commisison official said on Friday.

Farm Commisioner Franz Fischler put forward a new proposal this week to try to break the deadlock over the quota, designed to compensate the U.S. for trade lost due to enlargment of the European Union in 1995.
Implementation of the new duty free quota arrangments have been blocked because of fears that the U.S. tendering system would lead to cross subsidisation of rice exports.
The U.S. administration had proposed putting management of the quotas in the hands of a private group of rice exporters.
That, Commission officials say, could lead to profits from rice exports being used to finance more, free market, rice shipments to the EU.

"Commissioner Fischler has put a new proposal to the U.S. which would mean that tenders would be open to all producers in the U.S. A reply was expected this week but has not been received yet," an official said on Friday.
Under the quota arrangment the U.S. would be able to ship without duty 38,000 tonnes of milled rice and 8,000 tonnes of brown rice to the EU market.
